issue.title: [test] NTP tests fail on testbeds with ntpsec-based PTF containers (Debian 12+)

failure.body:
#### Description

NTP tests (`ntp/test_ntp.py`) fail with `NTP server was not started in PTF container` on any testbed where the PTF container runs **ntpsec** (Debian 12+ / Trixie) instead of classic `ntp`.

#### Root Cause

Two issues in `tests/common/helpers/ntp_helper.py`:

1. **`server <IP> prefer`** — ntpsec dropped support for the legacy refclock address syntax. The daemon silently ignores it, never synchronizes to the local clock, `ntpstat` returns rc≠0, and `check_ntp_status()` times out after 120s.

2. **`interface listen mgmt`** — standalone Docker PTF containers have no `mgmt` interface (only `eth0` veth pair). ntpsec starts but binds to no network interface, making port 123 unreachable.

#### Impact

All IPv4 NTP tests error during fixture setup:
- `test_ntp_long_jump_enabled[ipv4_allowed]`
- `test_ntp_long_jump_disabled[ipv4_allowed]`
- `test_ntp[ipv4_allowed]`

#### Environment

- PTF image: `docker-ptf:internal` (Debian 12, ntpsec 1.2.2)
- Testbed: BMC topology with standalone Docker PTF container
- sonic-mgmt: master branch (as of Aug 2026)

#### Fix

PR #27246

resolution.title: [test] Fix NTP helper for ntpsec on standalone Docker PTF containers
resolution.description:
#### Why I did it
Fixes #27247

The NTP test helper (`tests/common/helpers/ntp_helper.py`) fails on testbeds where the PTF container runs **ntpsec** (Debian 12+ / Trixie) instead of classic `ntp`:

1. `server <IP> prefer` — ntpsec dropped the legacy refclock address syntax; the daemon ignores it, `ntpstat` never reports synchronised, and `check_ntp_status` times out.
2. `interface listen mgmt` — standalone Docker PTF containers have no `mgmt` interface (only `eth0` veth pair); ntpsec starts but binds to nothing.

Both cause `NTP server was not started in PTF container` errors in `test_ntp.py`.

#### How I did it
- Probe for the `mgmt` interface (`ip link show mgmt`); skip interface restrictions when it doesn't exist.
- For ntpsec, use `refclock local stratum 3 prefer` (native syntax) and add `restrict <IP>` / `restrict ::1` so `ntpq` can query the daemon.
- Clean up new directives in teardown.

#### How to verify it
Run `ntp/test_ntp.py` against a testbed using a Docker PTF container with ntpsec (e.g., `docker-ptf:internal` based on Debian 12).

Before fix: 3 errors (`NTP server was not started`)
After fix: 3 passed, 3 skipped (IPv6 tests skip due to no IPv6 on PTF)
